rule_friction.idea: Build the SELL layouts in `fom_setup` through a public init routine in `src/fom_ops.c`, instead of lazily on the first `fom_iterate` call
rule_friction.rule: every function in fom_ops.c except the entry points must be static; fom_setup must not call fom_iterate
rule_friction.expected_gain: ~0 at steady state (only moves a one-time ~0.1 s setup out of the first solve)

rule_friction.idea: AVX2/AVX-512 gathers and FMA for the SELL kernels (`-march`)
rule_friction.expected_gain: unknown, likely small: Zen 4 gathers run about 1 element per cycle, close to the current scalar rate

rule_friction.idea: AVX2/AVX-512 kernels (FMA plus hardware gathers, which Ice Lake supports) through `-march` or `__attribute__((target))`
rule_friction.rule: fixed build flags / portable embedded target (the build is SSE2-only)
rule_friction.expected_gain: unknown, likely 1.3–2x on both product kernels

rule_friction.idea: Building the SELL layouts in `fom_setup` with a parallel first-touch, instead of lazily in the first `fom_iterate` call
rule_friction.rule: `fom_ops.c` may export only the listed entry points, and `fom_setup` may not call `fom_iterate`/`fom_step_*`
rule_friction.expected_gain: about 0 on the bench (setup falls in warmup), lower first-solve latency

rule_friction.idea: AVX2/FMA versions of the SELL gather and scatter kernels via `__attribute__((target("avx2,fma")))` with runtime CPU dispatch (4-wide value loads, fused multiply-add)
rule_friction.rule: the build flags are fixed (SSE2 baseline), and forcing a wider instruction set from the source would get around them
rule_friction.expected_gain: the kernels are bound by load and instruction count and take about 85% of the time, so I estimate 15–30% on them; not measured

rule_friction.idea: Compile the gather and scatter kernels with AVX2/FMA via `__attribute__((target))` plus a runtime CPU check, giving 256-bit value loads (fewer FP loads per entry) and FMA
rule_friction.rule: build flags are fixed (`-O3`, no `-march`), and per-function target attributes would amount to changing them, which also hurts portability on the embedded target
rule_friction.expected_gain: unknown, roughly 10-20% on the gather passes

rule_friction.idea: Inline-asm offset extraction (in-place `shr`/`movzwl`) to drop the register copies GCC adds
rule_friction.rule: x86-specific asm conflicts with portable embedded C under fixed flags

rule_friction.idea: Choose the reduction groups from the actual CPU-to-L3 topology (on AMD one group of four threads spans two L3 caches)
rule_friction.rule: needs OS topology queries (`sched_getcpu`, `/sys`) that don't belong in an allocation-free embedded solver
